extracted.intended_audience: independent public accountants auditing Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs), and SBIC boards/management
extracted.subtask_description: Audit and financial examination guidance for independent public accountants performing the annual audit of Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs) licensed by the SBA, including reporting, scope, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual audit requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: SBICs licensed by SBA are required to have an annual audit (financial examination) by independent public accountants as of the close of each Licensee’s approved fiscal year (ending March 31 unless SBA approves a different 12-month period). Three copies of the annual audit report should be submitted to SBA as soon as practicable and no later than the last day of the third month following the close of the period covered by the audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The engagement must cover a 'financial examination' type of audit described in the guide. If SBIC prefers, a detailed SBA Form 468 may be submitted separately or accompany the audit report (see guidance on optional long-form reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the independent public accountant
rubrics_metrics.description: Any public accountant certified or licensed by a regulatory authority of a State or comparable authority, truly independent and duly authorized to practice, may be considered qualified to render an opinion for an SBIC whose principal office is located in that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In jurisdictions not licensing public accountants, independent accountants of recognized standing with 10 or more years' public accounting experience selected or approved by SBA prior to September 8, 1967, may be similarly qualified if they satisfy SBA's requirements. The board selects the accountant, and SBA acceptance follows filing of the executed IPA Statement (Form 56) unless SBA advises otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA will not recognize an accountant as independent who is not in fact independent. An accountant is considered not independent if, during the period covered by the audit, he has any direct financial interest or any material indirect financial interest in the SBIC; or is connected as a promoter, underwriter, voting trustee, investment adviser, director, officer, employee, or is rendering bookkeeping services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA will consider all relevant circumstances and relationships between the accountant and the SBIC or affiliates and will not confine itself to relationships connected with filings to the Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for selection of the accountant
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of directors of the SBIC is responsible for selecting the independent public accountant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended the board give thorough consideration annually to the selection, agree on engagement terms and compensation, and notify the Office of Chief Accountant, SBA, of the selection (not necessary when the same accountant is retained for a succeeding year). The SBIC furnishes notification to SBA; accountant files executed IPA Statement (Form 56).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of a financial examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A financial examination includes: (1) review of the system of internal control and accounting principles followed; (2) independent testing (inspection, correspondence, confirmations, etc.) to ascertain existence of assets; (3) application of audit tests to ensure liabilities are reflected in the balance sheet in actual or approximate amounts; (4) review and testing of income and expense accounts; and (5) review of accounting records with appropriate testing to determine authenticity and general reliability of financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits shall be conducted in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards and include such tests of records and other procedures as deemed necessary to enable rendering an opinion on the statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit adjustments and treatment in report
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit adjustments are expected to be recorded in the SBIC's records before completion of the audit so that statements in the audit report agree with the books as adjusted to the balance sheet date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments included in audited statements but not agreed to by the SBIC and not recorded must be commented upon in the report. If no audit adjustments are recorded, the accountant should include narrative comments and qualifications necessary to disclose the SBIC's financial position. Recommended adjusting journal entries should be attached to each copy of the audit report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements and opinion applicability (Form 468)
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements to be reported upon should be those constituting the Financial Report, SBA Form 468. The accountant’s opinion in the audit report shall be made to apply to the specific financial statements and schedules constituting SBA Form 468 included in such audit report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If condensed statements are used in an optional report, they must, at minimum, include statement of financial condition, statement of surplus reconciliations, statement of income and expense, statement of realized gain or loss on investments, all presented to conform to SBA Form 468. The opinion must reference both the condensed statements and the Form 468 schedules included or accompanying the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit narrative comments and description of procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit narrative comments should include a concise but reasonably comprehensive description of the work done in addition to scope, a summation of findings on each significant balance sheet account and results of operations, and information on procedures employed in the audit of each significant account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be precise and meaningful; avoid stereotyping based on prior reports. When qualifying or disclaiming, cite specific loans/investments causing qualification and specific factors leading to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working papers access
rubrics_metrics.description: The engagement agreement between the SBIC and the accountant should provide that any information in the working papers will be made available upon request to the SBIC or to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the agreement explicitly permits SBIC or SBA access to working papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and additional communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Three copies of the audit report, with SBA Form 468 properly executed by appropriate officers, shall be submitted to SBA by the SBIC or by the accountant on behalf and with approval of the SBIC. Any matters for SBA attention not included in the audit report are to be set forth in an accompanying letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach recommended adjusting journal entries and copies of transmittal letters, special reports, summaries of recommendations, or similar communications to the inside back cover of each copy of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountant's certificate content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The accountant's certificate shall be dated, signed manually, identify without detailed enumeration the financial statements covered, state whether the audit was made in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards, and designate any generally recognized auditing procedures omitted and reasons for omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate shall clearly state: (a) the opinion as to accounting principles and fairness of presentation; (b) opinion as to material changes in accounting principles or practices affecting comparability; and (c) the nature and opinion as to any material differences between principles in the statements and those reflected in the accounts after entry of adjustments. Exceptions must be clearly identified and, to the extent practicable, the effect of each on related financial statements given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for reporting irregularities (defalcation/criminal violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any defalcation or other criminal violation is disclosed during the course of an audit, the independent public accountant must notify immediately the Office of Chief Accountant, SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA is vitally concerned and requires immediate notification—procedures should be in place to report such matters promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The accountant should review the company’s procedures and appraise the effectiveness of internal control. The extent and nature of testing and checking of certain accounts should be determined on the basis of this review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set forth observations on the effectiveness of internal control in general comments, and include suggestions for improvement where appropriate. Dual control is highlighted as a key feature of control arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish and maintain effective control arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee is required to establish and maintain effective control arrangements covering personnel, portfolio investment securities, funds, and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual control represents a key feature—accountant should note adherence and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity bond conformity check
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent public accountant should check the provisions of the SBIC’s fidelity bond against the requirements of SBA as stated in Addendum I of the guide, and should comment in the report regarding the conformity of the bond to such requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit commentary in the audit report about fidelity bond conformity is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the minutes of board meetings for the period under review to note items pertinent to the audit (elected officers, persons authorized to sign checks and execute legal/financial documents, dual control over disbursements and withdrawals, loans and equity purchases, sales, long-term financing, capital stock authorized, stock options, dividends, employment and remuneration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State in the report that minutes were reviewed, indicate whether they are up-to-date, and comment on any matters in the minutes worthy of attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash verification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash on hand should be counted. Cash in banks should be reconciled with book balances and confirmed by correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to bank statements at the balance sheet date, request and utilize cutoff statements as of a subsequent date to determine disposition of outstanding checks, deposits in transit, and other reconciling items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of U.S. government obligations, insured savings, and time deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary investments in direct and/or fully guaranteed U.S. Government obligations should be verified by inspection and, when applicable, by confirmation with custodians; verification should include ascertainment that coupons are attached to bearer bonds and that registered bonds are in the SBIC’s name or transferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded cost or current redemption value (for savings bonds) should be verified. Temporary investments in savings institutions should be reconciled and confirmed; time certificates of deposit examined to verify ownership and correctness of recorded balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes and accounts receivable confirmation and allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Miscellaneous notes, accounts receivable for services rendered, participating companies' portions, sales contracts, mortgages, and other evidences of indebtedness should be examined and reconciled to control accounts; representative items should be confirmed by correspondence as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate collectibility on basis of most reliable information, discuss with executive officers, recommend writeoffs for uncollectible items, provide for doubtful accounts in allowance, and include comments on adequacy of allowance in audit report. Confirm sales contracts and mortgages for proper recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accrued interest receivable and allowance adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine that interest receivable is currently and correctly accrued on the SBIC’s records for government obligations, loans, debt securities, notes receivable, sales contracts, and other interest-bearing amounts; review the allowance for uncollectible interest receivable and comment on adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include findings and recommendations regarding accruals and allowance in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances to directors, officers, and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Advances made to directors, officers, and employees should be reviewed for proper authorization and recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on these items in the report as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds in escrow and other current assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds in escrow pending closing of financing for small business concerns should be confirmed. Miscellaneous current assets should be reviewed for authenticity and appropriateness of classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify escrow documentation and ensure correct classification on the books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans and debt securities verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Review all notes, mortgages, and documents evidencing loans granted under section 305 and confirm directly with makers the unpaid balances; similarly examine and confirm debt securities purchased under section 304 and financings obtained from other SBICs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check obligation documents for signatures, proper witnessing and acknowledgment, stated interest rate and term. Confirm pledged loans and debt securities with holders. Ensure mortgages required to be recorded bear proper notation of recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participations inspection and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect each participation agreement under which the company has purchased a participation interest in a loan or debt security, inspect documents evidencing the participation, and request confirmation from sellers as necessary. Review subsidiary records of participations of others and confirm with purchasers to extent warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document inspections and confirmatory correspondence when participation balances are material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans and debt securities sold with recourse procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of loans and debt securities sold with recourse should be checked to records of such sales and to advices received from purchasers as to payments made by small business concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review current financial statements of concerns financed by the SBIC and provide comments; if such statements are not available, the accountant shall state so in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility for valuation and accountant review of valuation bases
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBIC board of directors has responsibility to determine in good faith a realistic valuation for each specific loan and debt security after considering all pertinent factors; valuation techniques and standards are set forth in SBA Policy and Procedural Release No. 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The independent public accountant should satisfy himself as to the reasonableness of the bases employed by the board in making valuation determinations, discuss valuations and any material decreases with executive officers, and ensure valuations are shown in the memorandum column of the applicable schedules of SBA Form 468.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for uncollectibles and losses on loans and debt securities
rubrics_metrics.description: The allowance for uncollectible loans and allowance for losses on debt securities should be reviewed as to adequacy and commented upon in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend adjusting entries to the allowance accounts or writeoffs where appropriate; give special attention to verification of unearned discount, fees, and other charges deducted from unpaid principal balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of unearned discount, fees, and other charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Special attention should be given to verification of all amounts of unearned discount, fees, and other charges shown as deducted from unpaid principal balances of loans and debt securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these deductions are supported by loan documents and calculations and are properly stated in accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital stock, warrants, options, and other stock rights verification
rubrics_metrics.description: All capital stock of small business concerns in the possession of the SBIC should be verified by inspection of stock certificates. Capital stock not in possession should be confirmed by correspondence with those having possession. Capital stock is to be recorded at cost on SBIC books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review cost determinations for warrants/options/stock rights carried at monetary value; inspect participation agreements and request confirmations from sellers as necessary; only the selling company’s portion is shown when participations sold to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of capital stock and stock rights and treatment of appreciation/depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of directors is responsible for determining in good faith realistic valuations for capital stock and stock rights after considering all pertinent factors. No appreciation in value of capital stock or stock rights is to be recorded in the books of account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountant should satisfy himself as to reasonableness of board bases; material decreases not obviously transitory should be compensated by increases in allowances for losses on capital stock or stock rights, and adjusting entries should be recommended.
